why: ONE backlog row in docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json, filed through scripts/ops/backlog_append.py so the file's exact serialisation round-trips. Nothing else changes. No src/, no config/, no tests/, no scripts/, no workflow, no order path, no strategy, no risk cap. Tier-1 by the canonical doc's own list, and CLAUDE.md states plainly that filing a backlog row is permitted with no cap because filing is the act of NOT taking the item.
landing_note: THIS IS ON ITS OWN BRANCH DELIBERATELY, AND THE REASON IS A MEASURED TRAP RATHER THAN TIDINESS. The finding was made while dispositioning the scope-overlap audit on PR #11896, so the tempting move was to add it there. Two rules forbid that and both are load-bearing: ONE PR = ONE concern, and CLAUDE.md's measured warning that once auto-merge is ARMED the branch must be treated as CLOSED to new content — on #11392 a commit pushed while CI ran on the previous head was NOT in the squash, because auto-merge took the earlier green head. #11896 is armed, so a row pushed there might simply never reach main while appearing to have been filed. The finding itself: scope-overlap-audit resolves a DIRECTORY declaration onto per-branch files (.github/pr-landing/<slug>.json, .github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt) whose whole design is that two branches cannot collide in them, so 7 of the 11 live-session rows it reported were structurally impossible collisions. Sole-writer measured with a positive control, not inferred from the naming convention.
